security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU's TCG translation of SCBNDSR (Set Bounds on Doubleword from Register) clears the capability tag when the requested bounds cannot be represented exactly, matching the incorrect pre-fix spec that conflated SCBNDSR with SCBNDS (Set Bounds on Doubleword from Scalar immediate). The fixed spec removes this tag-clearing rule from SCBNDSR — the instruction should NOT clear cd.tag due to inexact representability, only due to cs1.tag=0, cs1 being sealed, or cd bounds exceeding cs1 bounds. Keeping the stale rule in the emulator means a valid SCBNDSR operation that rounds representable bounds is incorrectly treated as a tag-clearing failure.
security_spec.summary: SCBNDSR/YBNDRW incorrecly clears cd.tag on inexact bounds encoding due to a spec copy-paste bug; the PR removes this spurious tag-clearing rule, and QEMU must mirror the fix to avoid wrongly invalidating capabilities.

findings.finding: CHERI SCBNDSR/SCBNDS capability bounds instructions are NOT implemented in this upstream qemu/qemu.git repository. No helper_scbndsr function, no CHERI CSR registers, no YBNDRW instruction decode entry, and no capability tag manipulation code exists under target/riscv/. The vulnerability pattern (scbndsr incorrectly clearing cd.tag due to inexact representability) cannot manifest because the instruction is not emulated at all.

spec_citations.excerpt: * SCBNDS sets the base to cs1.address, and the length to rs2. Set the ctag to zero if the bounds cannot be encoded exactly. * SCBNDSR sets the base to cs1.address, and the length to rs2. The bounds may be rounded up if they cannot be encoded exactly.
Set cd.tag=0 if cs1.tag=0, cs1 is sealed or if cd's bounds exceed cs1's bounds.
